headline: Democrats in holdout states eye Medicaid expansion
pages: Democrats in Georgia, Kansas and Texas see Medicaid expansion as a priority after winning legislative chambers and governors' seats in the midterms, Politico reported, as summarized by KFF Health News on Nov. 18. Georgia state Rep. Shea Roberts, a Democrat, called it low-hanging fruit.

Expansion would cover low-income adults without children or disabilities who do not qualify for traditional Medicaid. New Trump administration policies make expansion more costly and harder to run. Separately, Wyoming will receive more than $207 million for 2027 from the Rural Health Transformation Program.
